findings.summary: ASTM A53 is a carbon steel pipe specification covering seamless and welded types used for structural and low-pressure fluid conveyance. It is produced in three types—furnace-butt-welded, electric-resistance-welded, and seamless—each available in Grades A and B. The steel is made via open-hearth, electric-furnace, or basic-oxygen processes. Welded Grade B requires heat treatment to eliminate untempered martensite. The pipe is sized by the NPS system and commonly has threaded or plain ends for water, air, or steam service.

mechanisms.title: Weld seam tempering
mechanisms.explanation: For ASTM A53 Type E electric-resistance-welded Grade B pipe, the weld seam is heat treated after welding to a minimum of 1000 °F (540 °C) to ensure no untempered martensite remains.

mechanisms.title: Steel production process
mechanisms.explanation: The steel for both seamless and welded ASTM A53 pipe is made by open-hearth, electric-furnace, or basic-oxygen processes. If different grades are sequentially strand cast, transition material must be identified and removed.
